successCriteria.description: The service interface exposes exactly four operations — getPolicyForLeaveType, getActivePolicies, calculateEntitlement, validatePolicy — with signatures matching the LeavePolicy and LeaveTypeCode types from earlier phases; the concrete service class implements that interface.

calculateEntitlement implements the BINDING fiscal-year pro-ration rule: fiscal year starts Jan 1; a hireDate on or before Jan 1 of the fiscalYear yields the full entitlementDays; a hireDate within the fiscalYear is pro-rated by whole months remaining (11 minus the hire month), floored to an integer; a December hire yields 0; the optional maxAccumulation cap is applied after pro-ration when defined and exceeded.

getPolicyForLeaveType resolves a leave type by code, rejects a missing type with a NOT_FOUND error, rejects an inactive type with a POLICY_VIOLATION error, and rejects zero or multiple active policies for the type with a POLICY_VIOLATION error, returning the single active policy only on success.
getActivePolicies returns only policies whose isActive flag is true, returning an empty array when none are active, and propagates repository errors rather than swallowing them.

validatePolicy performs structural validation and returns a boolean (true only when all required fields are present and well-typed, optional fields are non-negative when defined, entitlementDays is a positive integer, and the boolean flags are booleans); it never throws — invalid input yields false.

The barrel index re-exports the service interface and the service class (plus the AppError error type) so downstream modules import the leave-policy service only through the module's public entry point.

A Jest unit test suite covers the pro-ration edge cases named in the phase scope — hire Jan 15 → 11 months, hire Dec 1 → 0 months, hire before the fiscal year → full — plus the Jan 1 boundary, the maxAccumulation cap, getPolicyForLeaveType error paths, getActivePolicies filtering, and validatePolicy positive/negative cases, all using mocked repositories.

constraints: The service must inject repository interfaces (ILeavePolicyRepository, ILeaveTypeRepository) and never touch the database directly — GP-001 repository pattern; no inline SQL or pool access inside the service.
No use of the any type — use unknown with type guards or explicit casts; strict TypeScript with strict null checks must pass (HARNESS no-any rule, severity high).

Modules import from each other only through their declared public entry point (index.ts); the service may import sibling model/interface files within its own module but cross-module consumers must go through the barrel.

All async errors must be caught and handled (GP-006); the service surfaces typed errors (AppError carrying a code string) for domain failures and propagates repository errors rather than leaving unhandled promise rejections.
calculateEntitlement is a pure synchronous function — it must not perform I/O or mutate its inputs; the same (policy, hireDate, fiscalYear) arguments always yield the same result.
outOfScope: LeaveBalanceService and balance initialization/reservation/deduction logic — Phase 9; this phase only exposes calculateEntitlement for Phase 9 to consume.
LeaveRequestService, routes, overlap detection, business-day counting, and the full leave-request lifecycle orchestration — Phase 10.
HTTP routes/controllers for leave-policy (upsertPolicy, getPolicyForType, getAllPolicies) and their RBAC enforcement — not part of this service-only phase.

Audit record creation for policy changes (GP-002) — the service performs read-only policy lookups and pure calculation; no state-changing operations occur in this phase, so no audit writes are required here.
Accrual scheduling, carryover/rollover, and use-it-or-lose-it enforcement across fiscal years — the binding rules describe these but they belong to the balance/accrual job phases, not this service.

entityInvariants.invariant: At most one active policy may exist per leave type for policy lookup to succeed; getPolicyForLeaveType treats zero or multiple active policies as a POLICY_VIOLATION, enforcing the single-active-policy-per-type invariant at read time.

Only an active LeaveType may back a policy lookup; an inactive type is rejected with POLICY_VIOLATION before any policy is resolved, preserving the rule that only active leave types and policies may be used.

A computed entitlement is always a non-negative integer: pro-ration floors the result, a December hire yields 0, and the maxAccumulation cap only ever lowers the value — it never produces a negative or fractional entitlement.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws a typed error with code NOT_FOUND when the leave type does not exist; throws a typed error with code POLICY_VIOLATION when the type is inactive or when zero or multiple active policies exist for the type; returns the single active LeavePolicy on success.
Returns the subset of all policies whose isActive is true (empty array if none); propagates repository errors unchanged rather than swallowing them.

Pure and deterministic: returns a non-negative integer; full entitlementDays when hireDate is on or before Jan 1 of the fiscalYear, else floor(entitlementDays * wholeMonthsRemaining / 12) with wholeMonthsRemaining = 11 - hireMonth (0 when ≤ 0), then capped at maxAccumulation when defined and exceeded; never throws on valid inputs.

Returns true only for a structurally valid policy (non-empty name/leaveTypeId, positive-integer entitlementDays, non-negative optional accrualRate/maxAccumulation/minimumNoticeDays, boolean flags); returns false for any invalid input and never throws — failures are caught and reported as false.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The service interface and implementation must reference the LeavePolicy shape exactly as defined in the Phase 3 model — entitlementDays, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, accrualRate, requiresManagerApproval, isActive — so calculateEntitlement and validatePolicy operate on the authoritative field names.
The service must call findByCode on ILeaveTypeRepository (Phase 2) to resolve a leave type by code; it must not re-implement type lookup or bypass the repository contract.

The service must call findActiveByLeaveTypeId and findAll on ILeavePolicyRepository (Phase 3) for policy retrieval; active-policy filtering for getActivePolicies is performed in application code against the isActive flag, matching the repository's returned shape.

The leaveTypeCode parameter type must be the LeaveTypeCode enum from shared-types (annual/sick/emergency/unpaid/maternity/paternity) — the service must not define a parallel code type or accept a raw string.

Error codes emitted by the service (NOT_FOUND, POLICY_VIOLATION) must match the Error Response Contract codes documented in the reconciled architecture so downstream controllers can map them to the agreed HTTP statuses (404, 400).

integrationPoints.why: calculateEntitlement is the contract Phase 9 consumes to initialize per-employee balances for each active policy using the employee's hireDate and the current fiscal year.
getPolicyForLeaveType and getActivePolicies are consumed by the request orchestrator to resolve the governing policy for minimum-notice, approval-flag, and entitlement checks during submit/approve.
Downstream modules (leave-balance, leave-request) must import ILeavePolicyService and LeavePolicyService only through the leave-policy public entry point, per the module-boundary rule.
